			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">EXPLANATORY NOTE</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Unless the context indicates otherwise, any reference in this report to &#x201C;EVHC,&#x201D; &#x201C;Envision Healthcare</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,&#x201D;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x201C;the Company,&#x201D; &#x201C;we,&#x201D; &#x201C;our,&#x201D; or &#x201C;us&#x201D; refer to Envision Healthcare Holdings,&nbsp;Inc. and its direct and indirect subsidiaries.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Envision Healthcare Corporation, formerly known as Emergency Medical Services Corporation, (&#x201C;Corporation&#x201D;) is a wholly</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;owned subsidiary of the Company. Corporation, previously a registrant under the Exchange Act, terminated its registration under the Exchange Act in June 2014. Our business is conducted primarily through two operating subsidiaries, EmCare Holdings,&nbsp;Inc. (&#x201C;EmCare&#x201D;) and American Medical Response,&nbsp;Inc.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, including its affiliates</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;AMR&#x201D;).</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We are a leading provider of physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led, medical services in the United States</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> offering</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> a broad range of clinically </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">based and coordinated care solutions across the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">patient continuum.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We manage a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">patient t</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">reatment cycle that includes healthcare transportation, hospital encounters and</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> comprehensive care alternatives in various settings. We believe that our capabilities </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">present</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> a powerful value proposition to healthcare facilities, communities and payors by helping to improve the quality of care and lower overall healthcare costs. We market our services on a stand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;alone, multi</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;service and integrated basis, primarily under our EmCare and AMR brands. EmCare, with 40&nbsp;years of operating history and more than 13,000 affiliated physicians and other clinicians, is a leading provider of integrated facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based physician services, including emergency, anesthesiology, hospitalist/inpatient care, radiology, tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology and surgery. EmCare also offers physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led care management solutions outside the hospital. AMR, with more than 55&nbsp;years of operating history and more than 20,000</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> paramedics and emergency medical technicians, is a leading provider and manager of community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based healthcare transportation services, including emergency (&#x201C;911&#x201D;), non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency, managed transportation, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">fire protection services, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wing air ambulance and disaster response.</font>

Evolution Health serves patients who require comprehensive care across various settings, many of whom suffer from advanced illnesses and chronic diseases. Our Evolution Health solutions leverage many of the competencies of EmCare and AMR, including clinical resource management, patient flow coordination, evidence</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based clinical protocols, community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based clinical and healthcare transportation services, patient monitoring and clinician recruitment.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">General Development of our Business</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Company History</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">EmCare was founded in Dallas, Texas in 1972 and initially grew by providing emergency department staffing and related management services to larger hospitals in the Texas marketplace. EmCare then expanded its presence nationally, primarily through a series of acquisitions in the 1990s. Over its 40</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;year operating history, EmCare has become a leading provider of integrated facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based physician services to healthcare facilities in the United States. EmCare has further expanded the Company&#x2019;s comprehensive care management solutions outside the hospital through Evolution Health.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Evolution Health was formed in 2012 through the combination of two acquired businesses, a provider of primary care physician healthcare services to patients at their place of residence with operations in Texas, and a post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;acute care services provider with operations in Indiana, Ohio, Oklahoma and Texas. We have subsequently expanded Evolution Health&#x2019;s service offerings and integrated its services with our other lines of business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 10pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">AMR was founded in 1992 through the consolidation of several well</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;establish</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ed regional ambulance companies</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> with more than 55&nbsp;years of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">combined </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">operating history, and has grown</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> both</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> organically and through acquisitions. In February 1997, AMR merged with another leading ambulance company and became a leading provider and manager of comm</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">unity</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based healthcare transportation services.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> On October 28, 2015, we completed our combination with Rural/Metro Corporation</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> (&#x201C;Rural/ Metro&#x201D;)</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, creating one of the premier providers of healthcare transportation services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Envision Healthcare Holdings, Inc.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> was formed in 2011 in connection with the acquisition of Corporation in a merger transaction (the &#x201C;Merger&#x201D;) by the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">investment funds sponsored by, or affiliated with, Clayton, Dubilier &amp; Rice, LLC (the &#x201C;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">CD&amp;R Affiliates</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x201D;)</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. In May 2011, in connection with the Merger, substantially all of the outstanding shares of common stock of the Company were purchased by the CD&amp;R Affiliates, and Corporation became an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> On August&nbsp;19, 2013, the Company completed its initial public offering.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">During 2014 and 2015 the Company registered the offering and sale of common stock by the CD&amp;R Affiliates, and on March 11, 2015, the CD&amp;R Affiliates disposed of their remaining shares of the Company&#x2019;s common stock in a registered secondary offering.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> As of December 31, 2015, Envision Healthcare Holdings, Inc. employs more than 49,000 employees and affiliated clinicians.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Description of our Business</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Industry Overview</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We operate in the facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based and post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;acute care physician services, and community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based healthcare transportation markets, two large and growing segments of the healthcare market that are supported by favorable demographics, including the growth and aging of the population. Our services are offered on a stand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;alone basis or as part of an integrated services program combining two or more services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Emergency Department (&#x201C;ED&#x201D;)</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide ED physician services to hospitals and other facilities. Facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based ED physician services providers such as EmCare are primarily focused on improving the patient experience and enhancing the quality of care at their customers&#x2019; healthcare facilities through broader physician access, physician retention and training programs, better management tools and risk mitigation expertise. In addition, we believe leading facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based physician services providers are well</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;positioned to improve operational efficiency, reduce hospital ED wait times and increase its productivity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe the physician reimbursement component of the ED services market represents annual expenditures of nearly $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">20</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;billion. The market for ED staffing and related management services is highly fragmented, with more </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">than 500 national</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, regional and local providers handling an estimated </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">136</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million patient visits in 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. There are </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5,000</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> hospitals in the United States that operate EDs, of which approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">70</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">contract</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> their ED physician staffing and management</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> to physician management organizations</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. We believe we are one of only </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">seven</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> national providers and the largest provider based on number of ED contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Between 2000 and 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, the total number of patient visits to hospital EDs increased </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">26</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% from approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">108</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million to approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">136</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million per annum. We believe that a portion of the historical and expected growth of ED visits is driven by the shortage of primary care physicians in the United States, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">which leads to access to care challenges, causing</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> many patients to utilize the ED as their primary source for</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> accessing the</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> healthcare</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> system</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. This trend, combined with a decline in the number of hospital EDs, has resulted in a substantial increase in the average number of patient visits per hospital ED during this period. In addition, the Patient Protection and Affordable Ca</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">re Act (&#x201C;PPACA&#x201D;) </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">provide</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> healthcare coverage to previously uninsured individuals through the expansion of state Medicaid programs and the creation of federal and state healthcare exchanges, which we anticipate will increase overall utilization and reimbursement for ED services. We believe increased volumes through EDs and cost pressures facing hospitals have resulted</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and will result in</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> an increased focus by facilities on improving the op</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">erating efficiency of their EDs. This is</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> a core competency of EmCare.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Hospitalist Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide inpatient physician services, or hospitalists, for patients who are admitted to hospitals and either have no primary care physician or the attending physician requests that our hospitalist manage the patient. This program benefits hospitals by optimizing the average length of stay for patients and can improve patient flow and care coordination through effective working relationships with EDs. Inpatient service physicians are also an integral part of the post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;discharge coordination of patient care by directing how care outside the hospital setting should be established and coordinated. Certain studies indicate better patient outcomes and lower costs with these hospitalist programs. The market for this healthcare specialty, with estimated annual expenditures of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;billion, is expected to continue to grow as hospitals face additional cost pressures and added focus on improving patient outcomes. This market is currently serviced by </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">national, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">regional and local providers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Anesthesiology Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide anesthesiology services to hospitals, free</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;standing ambulatory surgery centers and physician offices. These services are performed by anesthesiologists and certified registered nurse anesthetists. Anesthesiologists are a key part of the effective management and productivity of surgery departments and free</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;standing ambulatory surgery centers. These clinicians can have a significant impact on surgeon satisfaction, which is crucial to the financial viability of the surgery department in hospitals and free</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;standing ambulatory surgery centers. The anesthesiology market is estimated to have annual expenditures of approximately $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">19&nbsp;b</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">illion and is currently serviced primarily by hospitals, which self</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;operate their programs, and by local providers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Radiology/Tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide radiology, including tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology, services to hospitals. The industry for these services comprises a number of smaller local and regional groups, which are at a disadvantage compared to national providers having the ability to recruit, train and leverage existing capital and infrastructure support. Tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology, the process whereby digital radiologic images are sent from one point to another, has become a fast</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;growing healthcare service. This technology allows hospitals to have access to full</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;time radiology support, even when access to full</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;time radiologists on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;site may be limited. The market for radiology and tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology service</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">s</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> has estimated annual expenditures of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$18</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;billion and is currently serviced primarily by hospitals, which self</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;operate their programs, and by local providers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Surgery Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We offer management, oversight and surgeon staffing for trauma surgery services. This service gives hospitals the opportunity to raise their trauma designation by providing expanded coverage and management for surgery services. While the market for this service is still emerging, we estimate annual expenditures of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$2</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;billion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Post-acute Management of Patient Populations</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We expanded our</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led services outside the hospital through the formation of Evolution Health</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> in 2012</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. Evolution Health provides comprehensive care management solutions through a suite of physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led services, including transitional care teams, direct patient care and care coordination by clinicians outside the acute</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;care setting, as well as tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;monitoring and tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;medicine. Evolution Health serves patients who require comprehensive care across various settings, many of whom suffer from advanced illnesses and chronic diseases. We believe that leading providers of care management solutions outside the hospital can offer an attractive value </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">proposition. Our business model</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> helps payors reduce their cost of care, promote the most appropriate care in the most appropriate setting, identify member health risks, enable self</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;care and independence at home, and reduce hospital lengths of stay and readmissions. For hospitals, we believe leading providers can improve patient flow coordination, decrease lengths of stay and reduce readmission rates. While our Evolution Health solutions continue to be implemented, the expansion of our Evolution Health business is a key element of our business strategy for future growth. We believe the addressable market for care management solutions outside the hospital represents annual expenditures of approximately $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">64</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;billion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Ambulance Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Ambulance services encompass both &#x201C;9</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">11&#x201D; emergency response and non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">emergency transport services, including critical care transfers, wheelchair transports and other inter</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;facility transports. Emergency response services include the dispatch of ambulances equipped with life support equipment and staffed with paramedics and/or emergency medical technicians (&#x201C;EMTs&#x201D;) to provide immediate medical care to injured or ill patients. Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency services utilize paramedics, EMTs and/or nurses to transport patients between healthcare facilities or between facilities and patient residences.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response services are provided primarily under exclusive long</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;term contracts with communities and government agencies which by law are generally required to provide such services. These contracts typically specify maximum fees a provider may charge and set forth minimum requirements, such as response times, staffing levels, types of vehicles and equipment, quality assurance and insurance coverage. The rates that a provider is permitted to charge for services under a contract for &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency ambulance services and the amount of the subsidy, if any, the provider receives from a community or government agency depend in large part on the nature of the services it provides, the payor mix and the performance requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency services generall</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">y are provided pursuant to non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">exclusive contracts with healthcare facilities and payors. Usage tends to be controlled by the facility discharge planners, nurses and physicians who are responsible for requesting transport services. Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency services are provided primarily by private ambulance companies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe that the ambulance services market, including both emergency and non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency transports, represents annual expenditures of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately $18&nbsp;billion. The ambulance services market is highly fragmented, with more than 15,000 private, public and not</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;for</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;profit service providers accounting for an estimated 45&nbsp;million ambulance transports in 2015. There are a limited number of regional ambulance providers, and we are the largest</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> national ambulance provider based on net revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Managed Transportation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide managed transportation administration services to insurers, government entities and healthcare providers. Through partnerships with external transportation providers, our services include managing ambulance, wheelchair and other types of transportation to provide a cost</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;effective solution for those we serve. We believe the managed transportation market represents annual expenditures of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately $2&nbsp;billion</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Industrial and Community Fire Protection Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> fire protection services to airports, industrial facilities and communities, as well as, individual homeowners and commercial property owners in unincorporated communities not included within municipal fire department boundaries. Through partnerships with cities, towns and fire districts we also provide a full complement of fire protection, prevention and emergency medical services.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Wing Air Transport Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We also provide fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wing air ambulance transport services, including the specialized medical care required by patients during the transports. Our services focus on patients who require longer travel distances to retain the appropriate care, both in emergency and non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency situations. Additionally,&nbsp;we offer international repatriation services for emergency medical needs. We believe the medical air transportation market represents annual expenditures of approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">$3&nbsp;billion.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Reportable </font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Business Segments and Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">currently </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">operate our business and market our services under our two business segments: EmCare and AMR. We provide integrated facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based and post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;acute care physician services in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">42</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> states and the District of Columbia and provide and manage healthcare transportation services in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">39</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> states and the District of Columbia.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The following is a detailed business description for our two </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">reportable </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">business segments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">EmCare</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">EmCare is a leading provider of integrated facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based and post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;acute care physician services to healthcare facilities in the United States. EmCare has contracts covering </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">over 900</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> clinical departments with hospitals and independent physician groups to provide emergency, anesthesiology, hospitalist/inpatient care, radiology, tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology and surgery services as well as other administrative services. During 201</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, EmCare had approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">18.0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million weighted patient encounters in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">42</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> states and the District of C</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">olumbia. As of December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, EmCare had a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the total ED services market and a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">14</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the ED services market, the largest share among providers based on number of contracts. EmCare&#x2019;s share of the combined markets for anesthesiology, hospitalist, radiology and surgery services was </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately 1%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> as of such date.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We recruit and hire or subcontract with physicians and other healthcare professionals, who then provide services to patients in the facilities with whom we contract. EmCare bills and collects from each patient or the patient&#x2019;s insurance provider for the medical services performed. We also have practice support agreements with independent physician groups and hospitals pursuant to which we provide management services such as billing and collection, recruiting, risk management and certain other administrative services.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Contract Management.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We utilize an integrated approach to contract management that involves physicians, non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;clinical business experts and operational and quality assurance specialists. An on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;site medical director responsible for the day</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;to</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;day oversight of the relationship, including clinical quality, works closely with the facility&#x2019;s management in developing strategic initiatives and objectives. A</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> quality manager develops site</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">specific quality improvement programs, and a practice improvement staff focuses on chart documentation, operational improvement and physician utilization patterns. The regional</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based management staff provides support for these efforts and ensures that each customer&#x2019;s expectations are identified, that service plans are developed and executed to meet those expectations, and that the customer&#x2019;s financial objectives and ours are achieved.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Staffing.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We provide a full range of staffing services to meet the unique needs of each healthcare facility. Our dedicated clinical teams include qualified physicians and other healthcare professionals responsible for the delivery of high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;quality, cost</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;effective care. These teams also rely on managerial personnel, many of whom have clinical experience, who oversee the administration and operations of the clinical area. Ensuring that each contract is staffed with the appropriate mix of qualified physicians and other medical professionals and that coverage is provided without any service deficiencies is critical to the success of the contract.</font>

Our marketing and recruiting staff continuously up</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">dates our database of more </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">than 950,000 physicians with</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> relevant data and contact information to allow us to match potential physician candidates to specific openings based upon personal preferences. This targeted recruiting method increases the success and efficiency of our recruiters, and we believe significantly increases our physician retention rates.</font>

Our website is optimized for easy navigation and enables interested providers to quickly view positions either by specialty or geograph</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">y. Our in-house team of subject-</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">matter experts diligently monitors the performance of all recruiting initiatives.&nbsp; </font>

We provide 24</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;hour service to ensure that unscheduled situations such as physician illness and personal emergencies do not result in a disruption of coverage.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Operational Improvement Assessments.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;On behalf of our hospital customers, we implement process improvement programs that are directed toward enhancement of operating and triage systems, and improvement of critical operational metrics, including turnaround times, &#x201C;left without being treated&#x201D;, and throughput times. Through an initial assessment, we establish baseline values, which are used to develop and implement process improvement programs, and then we monitor the success of the initiatives. We also design and implement customized patient satisfaction programs for our hospital customers. These programs are delivered to the clinical and non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;clinical members of the hospital ED as well as other areas of a healthcare facility where services are being provided.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Practice Support Services.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We provide a substantial portion of our services to healthcare facilities through our affiliate physician groups. However, in some situations facilities and physicians are interested in receiving stand</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;alone management services such as billing and collection, scheduling, recruitment and risk management, and at times we unbundle our services to meet these needs. Pursuant to these practice support agreements, which generally will have a term of one to three years, we provide these services to independent physician groups and healthcare facilities.</font>

We provide comprehensive care management solutions through a suite of physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led techniques and services, including transitional care teams, direct patient care and care coordination by clin</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">icians outside the acute</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">care setting, tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;monitoring and tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;medicine. We market these services to payors and healthcare systems.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We utilize our risk management function, se</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">nior medical leadership and on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">site medical directors to conduct aggressive risk management and quality assurance programs. We take a proactive role in promoting early reporting, evaluation and resolution of incidents that may evolve into claims. Our risk management function is designed to mitigate risk associated with the delivery of care and to prevent or minimize costs associated with medical professional liability claims and includes:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Incident Reporting Systems.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have established a comprehensive support system for medical professionals. Our Risk Management Hotline provides each physician with the ability to discuss medical issues with a peer, an attorney or a risk management specialist.</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Tracking and Trending Claims.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We utilize an extensive claims database developed from our experience in the ED setting to identify claim trends and risk factors so that we can better target our risk management initiatives. Periodically, we target the medical conditions associated with our most frequent professional liability claims, and provide detailed education to assist our affiliated medical professionals in treating these medical conditions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Professional Risk Assessment.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We conduct risk assessments of our medical professionals. Typically, a risk assessment includes a thorough review of professional liability claims against the professional, assessment of issues raised by hospital risk management and identification of areas where additional education may be advantageous for the professional.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Hospital Risk Assessment.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We conduct risk assessments of potential hospital customers in conjunction with our sales and contracting process. As part of the risk assessment, we conduct a detailed analysis of the hospital&#x2019;s operations affecting the services of our affiliated medical professionals, including the triage procedures, on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;call coverage, transfer procedures, nursing staffing and related matters in order to address risk factors contractually during negotiations with potential customer hospitals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Clinical Fail</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Safe Programs.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We review and identify key risk areas which we believe may result in increased incidence of patient injuries and resulting claims against us and our affiliated medical professionals. We have developed &#x201C;fail</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;safe&#x201D; clinical tools and make them available to our affiliated physicians for use in conjunction with their practice. These &#x201C;fail</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;safe&#x201D; tools assist physicians in identifying common patient attributes and complaints that may identify the patient as being at high risk for certain conditions such as a heart attack.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Professional Liability Claims Committee.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Each professional liability claim brought against an EmCare affiliated medical professional or EmCare affiliated company is reviewed by EmCare&#x2019;s Claims Committee, consisting of physicians, attorneys and company executives, before any resolution of the claim. The Claims Committee periodically instructs EmCare&#x2019;s risk management personnel to undertake an analysis of particular physicians or hospital locations associated with a given claim.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Insurance</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Professional Liability Program.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;From January&nbsp;1, 2002</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> through the present, our professional liability insu</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">rance program provides &#x201C;claims</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">made&#x201D; insurance coverage with a limit of $1&nbsp;million per loss event and a $3&nbsp;million annual per provider aggregate, for all medical professionals whom we have agreed to cover under our professional liability insurance program. In addition, from time to time, we contract with insurance providers outside of our insurance program, customarily when the third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party provider can provide economically more favorable terms to our insurance program for a specific specialist practice, or if it is a legacy provider from acquisitions. Our subsidiaries and affiliated corporate entities are provided with coverage of $1&nbsp;million per loss event and share a $10&nbsp;million annual corporate aggregate.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">From 2002 through the present, most of our professional liability insurance coverage was provided by affiliates of Columbia Casualty Company and Continental Casualty Company (collectively, &#x201C;CCC&#x201D;). The CCC policies have a retroactive date of January&nbsp;1, 2001, thereby covering all claims occurring during the 2001 calendar year but reported in each of the following calendar years.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We code and bill for most of our ED and hospitalist physician services through our wholly owned subsidiary, Reimbursement Technologies,&nbsp;Inc</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. We utilize</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> paperless workflow processes to expedite the billing cycle and improve compliance and customer service. Coding and billing for our anesthesiology and radiology services is provided by a combination of internal and externa</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">l billing companies. Certain ED, hospitalist and physician </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">services</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">are also billed by external billing companies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We do substantially all of the billing for our affiliated physicians, and we have extensive experience in processing claims to third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and patients</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. We employ a billing staff of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately 900 employees</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> who are trained in third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party coverage and reimbursement procedures. Our integrated billing and collection system uses proprietary software to prepare the submission of claims to Medicare, Medicaid and certain other third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors based on the payor&#x2019;s reimbursement requirements and has the capability to electronically submit most claims to the third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors&#x2019; systems. We forward uncollected accounts electronically to outside collection agencies automatically, based on established parameters. Each of these collection agencies have on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;site employees working at our in</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;house billing company to assist in providing patients with quality customer service.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Reimbursement for our EmCare physician services has historically been stable. In addition, in many of our hospital contracts, we have had the ability to obtain or </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">modify</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> subsidies to offset any reimbursement or payor mix changes. Further, we typically have visibility into payor mix prior to entering into new contracts, and our payor mix has been stable over time, which allows us to more effectively manage exposure to each payor category.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Contracts</font>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We deliver services to our hospital customers and their patients through two principal types of contractual arrangements. EmCare or a subsidiary most frequently contracts directly with the hospital to provide physician staffing and management services. In some instances, a physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;owned professional corporation contracts with the hospital to provide physician staffing and management services, and the professional corporation, in turn, contracts with us for a wide range of management and administrative services including billing, scheduling support, accounting and other services. The professional corporation pays our management fee </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">from</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> the fees it collects from patients, third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors and, in some cases, the hospital customer. Our physicians and other healthcare professionals who provide services under these hospital contracts do so pursuant to independent contractor or employment agreements with us, or pursuant to arrangements with the professional corporation that has a management agreement with us. We refer to all of these physicians as our affiliated physicians, and these physicians and other individuals as our healthcare professionals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Hospital and Practice Support Contracts.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Generally, agreements with hospitals are awarded on a competitive basis, and have an initial term of three years with one</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;year automatic renewals and termination by either party on specified notice.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our contracts with hospitals provide for one of three payment models:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">we bill patients and third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#8209;party payors directly for physician fees, with the hospital paying us an additional pre</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#8209;arranged fee for our services, or</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We bill patients and third-party payors for physician-related services, what is often referred to as the &#x201C;professional component&#x201D;. Separately, hospitals and other allied health providers bill the same patients and third-party payors for services they provide, including medical equipment and diagnostic testing.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In all cases, the hospitals are responsible for billing and collecting for non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;related services as well as for providing the capital for medical equipment and supplies associated with the services we provide.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We have established long</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;term relationships with some of the largest healthcare </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">facilities </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">providers in the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">country. As of December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, EmCare had contracts covering </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">over 900 clinical departments, with patient revenue generated at t</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">he top 10 contracts representing only </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of EmCare net revenue. One customer, Hospital Corporation of America, comprised </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">24.1</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% o</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">f EmCare&#x2019;s total net revenue for the twelve months ended December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. We have maintained our relationships with these customers for an average of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Affiliated Physician Group Contracts.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;In most states, we contract directly with our hospital customers to provide physician staffing and related management services. We, in turn, contract with a professional corporation that is wholly owned by one or more physicians, which we refer to as an affiliated physician group, or with independent contractor physicians. It is these physicians who provide the medical professional services. We then provide comprehensive management services to the physicians. We typically provide professional liability and workers compensation coverage to our affiliated physicians.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Certain states have laws that prohibit or restrict unlicensed persons or business entities from practicing medicine. The laws vary in scope and application from state to state. Some of these states may prohibit us from contracting directly with hospitals or physicians to provide professional medical services. In those states, the affiliated physician groups contract with the hospital, as well as all medical professionals. We provide management services to the affiliated physician groups.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Medical Professional Contracts.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We contract with healthcare professionals as either independent contractors or employees to provide services to our customers. The healthcare professionals generally are paid an hourly rate for each hour of coverage, a variable rate based upon productivity or other objective criteria or a combination of both a fixed hourly rate and a variable rate component. We typically arrange for professional liability and workers compensation coverage for our healthcare professionals.</font>
		</p>

The contracts can be terminated with cause for various reasons, and usually contain provisions allowing for termination without cause by either party upon 90&nbsp;days&#x2019; notice. Agreements with physicians generall</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">y contain a non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;compete or non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">solicitation provision and, in the case of medical directors, a non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;compete provision. The enforceability of these provisions varies from state to state.</font>

We have developed and implemented several proprietary applications that we believe provide us with a competitive advantage in our operations.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Intellectual Property</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We have registered the trademark EmCare</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, certain other trademarks</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and the EmCare logo in the United States. Generally, registered trademarks have perpetual life, provided that they are renewed on a timely basis and continue to be used properly as trademarks. We have also developed proprietary technology that we protect through contractual provisions and confidentiality procedures and agreements. Other than the EVHC and EmCare trademarks and the EmTrac, EmComp and EmBillz software, we do not believe our business is dependent to a material degree on patents, copyrights, trademarks or trade secrets. Other than licenses to commercially available software, we do not believe that any of our licenses to third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party intellectual property are material to our business taken as a whole.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Sales and Marketing</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Contracts for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">staffing and related management</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based services are obtained through strategic marketing programs and responses to requests for proposal (&#x201C;RFPs&#x201D;). EmCare&#x2019;s business development team includes Practice Development representatives located throughout the United States who are responsible for developing sales and acquisition opportunities for the operating group within a specific territory. A significant portion of the compensation program for these sales professionals is commissions, based on the profitability of the contracts they sell. Leads are generated through regular marketing efforts by our business development group, our website, journal advertising, conventions and a lead referral program. Each Practice Development representative is responsible for working with the regional chief executive officer to structure and provide customer proposals for new prospects in their respective regions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">A healthcare facility RFP generally will include demographic information of the facility department, a list of services to be performed, the length of the contract, the minimum qualifications of bidders, billing information, selection criteria and the format to be followed in the bid. Prior to responding to an RFP, EmCare&#x2019;s senior management ensures that the proposal is consistent with certain financial parameters. Senior management evaluates all aspects of each proposal, including financial projections, staffing model, resource requirements and competition, to determine how to best achieve our business objectives and the customer goals.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Competition</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The market for ED staffing and related management services is highly fragmented, with more than </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">500</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> national, regional and local providers handling an estimated </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">136</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million patient visits in 201</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. There are </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5,000</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> hospitals in the United States that operate EDs, of which approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">70</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">contract with third-party physician management organizations for</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ED physician staffing and management. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">35%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of these hospitals </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">contract with a local provider, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% contract with a regional provider and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">26</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% contract with a national provider based on estimated net revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Team Health is our largest competitor and has the second largest share of the ED services market with an approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">8</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share based on number of contracts. Other </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">large</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> providers of ED </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">staffing </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">services are Hospital Physician Partners, Schumacher Group and California Emergency Physicians.</font>
		</p>

For anesthesiology services, we have a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> share of the market with an additional </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% market share split between Team Health, Sheridan Healthcare, Premier Anesthesia, North American Partners in Anesthesia and NorthStar Anesthesia. Other national providers are Team Health</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, Sound Physicians and Apogee.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> For radiology services, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">there are </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">four other national providers</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, which</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> each have a market share similar to ours at </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe that our relations with our employees and independent contractors are good. None of EmCare&#x2019;s physicians, physician assistants, nurse practitioners or non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;clinical employees is subject to any collective bargaining agreement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We offer our physicians substantial flexibility in terms of type of facility, scheduling of work hours, benefit packages, opportunities for relocation and career development. This flexibility, combined with fewer administrative burdens, improves physician retention rates and stabilizes our contract base.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">AMR</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">AMR has developed the largest network of ambulance services and a leading position in other healthcare transportation services in the United States. AMR and our predecessor companies have been providing services to some communities for more than 5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">0&nbsp;years. As of December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we had a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the total ambulance services market and a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">private</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ambulance market. During 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, AMR treated and transported approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">3.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million patients in </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">39</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> states and the District of Columbia utilizing over </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">4,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">900</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> vehicles that operated out of over </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">275</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> sites. AMR has more than </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5,000</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> contracts with communities, government agencies, healthcare providers and insurers to provide ambulance transport services. AMR&#x2019;s broad geographic footprint enables us to contract on a national and regional basis with insurance companies, healthcare facilities and government agencies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">During 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">58</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of AMR&#x2019;s net revenue was generated from emergency &#x201C;911&#x201D; ambulance services. These services include treating and stabilizing patients, transporting the patient to a hospital or other healthcare facility and providing attendant medical care en route. Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency ambulance services, including critical care transfers, wheelchair transports and other interfacility transports, accounted for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of AMR&#x2019;s net revenue for the same period. The remaining</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> balance of net revenue for 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> was generated from managed transportation services, fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wing air ambulance services and the provision of training, dispatch and other services to communities and public safety agencies including services provided to FEMA.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">AMR has a national contract with FEMA</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> to provide ambulance and para</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">transit services, as well as rotary and fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wing air ambulance transportation services to supplement federal and military responses to disasters, acts of terrorism and other public health emergencies in the full 48 contiguous states.</font>
		</p>
