		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">See Item&nbsp;7, &#x201C;Management&#x2019;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations&#x201D; for further information on AMR&#x2019;s financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide substantially all of our healthcare transportation services under our AMR brand name. We operate under other names when required to do so by local statute or contractual agreement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Services</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We provide a full range of emergency and non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency ambulance transport and related services, which include:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#x201C;911&#x201D; Response Services.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We provide emergency response services primarily under long</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;term exclusive contracts with communities and hospitals. Our contracts typically stipulate that we must respond to &#x201C;911&#x201D; calls in the designated area within a specified response time. We utilize two types of ambulance units: Advanced Life Support (&#x201C;ALS&#x201D;) units and Basic Life Support (&#x201C;BLS&#x201D;) units. ALS units, which are staffed by two paramedics or one paramedic and an EMT, are equipped with high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;acuity life support equipment such as cardiac monitors, defibrillators and oxygen delivery systems, and carry pharmaceutical and medical supplies. BLS units are generally staffed by two EMTs and are outfitted with medical supplies and equipment necessary to administer first aid and basic medical treatment. The decision to dispatch an ALS or BLS unit is determined by our contractual requirements, as well as by the nature of the patient&#x2019;s medical situation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Under certain of our &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response contracts, we are the first responder to an emergency scene. However, under most of our &#x201C;911&#x201D; contracts, the local fire department is the first responder. In these situations, the fire department typically begins stabilization of the patient. Upon our arrival, we continue stabilization through the provision of attendant medical care and transport the patient to the closest appropriate healthcare facility. In certain communities where the fire department historically has been responsible for both first response and emergency services, we seek to develop public/private partnerships with fire departments to provide the emergency transport service. These partnerships emphasize collaboration with the fire departments and afford us the opportunity to provide &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency services in communities that, for a variety of reasons, may not otherwise have </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">contracted</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> this service to a private provider. In most instances, the provision of emergency services under our partnerships closely resembles that of our most common &#x201C;911&#x201D; contracts described above. The public/private partnerships lower our costs by reducing the number of full</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;time paramedics we would otherwise require. We estimate that the &#x201C;911&#x201D; contracts that encompass these public/private partnerships represented approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">11%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of AMR&#x2019;s net revenue for 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Emergency Healthcare Transportation Services.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We provide transportation to patients requiring ambulance or wheelchair transport with varying degrees of medical care needs between healthcare facilities or between healthcare facilities and their homes. Unlike emergency response services, which typically are provided by communities or private providers under exclusive or semi</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;exclusive contracts, non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency transportation usually involves multiple contract providers at a given facility, with one or more of the competitors designated as the &#x201C;preferred&#x201D; provider. Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency transport business generally is awarded by a healthcare facility, such as a hospital or nursing home, or a healthcare payor, such as an HMO, managed care organization or insurance company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Critical care transports are provided to medically unstable patients, such as cardiac patients and neonatal patients who require critical care while being transported between healthcare facilities. Critical care services differ from ALS services in that the ambulance may be equipped with additional medical equipment and may be staffed by one of our critical care nurses, respiratory therapists, or specially trained critical care paramedics, medical specialists or by an employee of a healthcare facility to attend to a patient&#x2019;s specific medical needs.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

				<font style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Symbol;border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9;font-size:10pt;;"> &#xB7;</font>
			</p>
		</td><td style="width:1pt;"><p style="width:1pt;width:1pt;font-size:0pt;"></p></td><td align="left" valign="top">
			<p style="border-top:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;border-bottom:1pt none #D9D9D9 ;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">Wheelchair and stretcher</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#8209;car transports are non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#8209;healthcare transportation provided to handicapped and certain non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">&#8209;ambulatory persons in some service areas. In providing this service, we use vans that contain hydraulic wheelchair lifts or ramps operated by drivers who generally are trained in cardiopulmonary resuscitation.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Medical Personnel and Quality Assurance</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Approximately 77%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of our </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">estimated </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">27,4</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">00</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> employees have daily contact with patients, including approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">8,580</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> paramedics, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">12,190</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> EMTs and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">420</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> nurses. Paramedics and EMTs must be state</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;certified and locally credentialed to transport patients and perform emergency care services. Certification as an EMT typically requires completion of approximately 150&nbsp;hours of training in a program designated by the U.S. Department of Transportation, such as those offered at our training institute, NCTI. Paramedic training involves over 1,000&nbsp;hours of didactic and clinical education focused on advanced levels of care. In addition, specialized courses may be completed to target specific patient populations (such as pediatrics, geriatrics, trauma, burns, etc).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">In most communities, the local physician medical director (often in conjunction with a physician advisory board) develops medical protocols to be followed by paramedics and EMTs in a service area. In addition, real</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;time instructions are conveyed on a case</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;by</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;case basis through direct communications between the ambulance crew and hospital emergency physicians. This consultation allows for more comprehensive evaluation and treatment of difficult cases. Like physicians, both paramedics and EMTs must complete continuing education programs and, in some cases, state supervised refresher training and/or examinations to maintain their certifications.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">AMR has a strong commitment to provide high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;quality pre</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209; and post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;hospital emergency medical care. Our focus on patient care is based on the published medical literature, participation with leading academic medical centers throughout the country, affiliation with international efforts to improve clinical care in emergency medical services (&#x201C;EMS&#x201D;), and our innovative approach known as AMR Medicine. In each individual location in which we provide services, a physician associated with a hospital we serve monitors adherence to medical protocol and conducts periodic audits of the care provided. In addition, we hold retrospective care audits with our employees to evaluate compliance with medical and performance standards. Our participation and leadership in national EMS organizations underscores the importance of our philosophy on patient care.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Of note, our commitment to quality is also reflected in the fact that a number of our operations across the country are accredited by the Commission on Accreditation of Ambulance Services (&#x201C;CAAS&#x201D;), representing </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">23</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of the total CAAS accredited centers. CAAS is a joint program between the American Ambulance Association and the American College of Emergency Physicians. The accreditation process is voluntary and evaluates numerous qualitative factors in the delivery of services. We believe communities and managed care providers increasingly consider accreditation as one of the criteria in awarding contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 12pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">See &#x201C;Business&#x2014;Regulatory Matters&#x2014;Medicare, Medicaid and Other Government Reimbursement Programs&#x201D; for additional information on reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid and other government</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;sponsored programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We have substantial experience overseeing the</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> processing of claims to third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">party payors and utilize billing consultants, trained in third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party coverage and reimbursement procedures. Our integrated billing and collection systems allow us to prepare the submission of claims to Medicare, Medicaid and certain other third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors based on the payor&#x2019;s reimbursement requirements, and have the capability to electronically submit claims to the extent third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors&#x2019; systems permit. These systems also provide for tracking of accounts receivable and status of pending payments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Companies in the ambulance services industry maintain significant provisions for doubtful accounts, or uncompensated care, compared to companies in other industries. Collection of complete and accurate patient billing information during an emergency service call is sometimes difficult, and incomplete information hinders post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;service collection efforts. In addition, we cannot evaluate the creditworthiness of patients requiring emergency healthcare transportation services. Our provision for uncompensated care generally is higher for transports resulting from emergenc</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">y ambulance calls than for non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">emergency ambulance requests. See Item&nbsp;1A, &#x201C;Risk Factors&#x2014;Risk Factors Related to Healthcare Regulation&#x2014;Changes in</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> the rates or methods of third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">party reimbursements, including due to political discord in the budgeting process outside our control, may adversely affect our revenue and operations.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">State licensing requirements, as well as contracts with communities and healthcare facilities, typically require us to provide ambulance services without regard to a patient&#x2019;s insurance coverage or ability to pay. As a result, we often receive partial or no compensation for services provided to patients who are not covered by Medicare, Medicaid or private insurance. The anticipated level of uncompensated care and uncollectible accounts is considered in negotiating a government</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;paid subsidy to provide for uncompensated care, and permitted billing rates under contracts with a community or government agency.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">As a &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response provider, we are uniquely positioned for stable pricing as changes in reimbursement from Medicare or other payors can typically be offset by requesting increases in the rates we are permitted to charge for &#x201C;911&#x201D; services from the communities we serve. Communities and municipalities set these emergency allowable rates for commercial payors and, with limited exceptions, do not pay for services out of the tax base. These communities often permit us to increase rates for ambulance services from patients and their third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors in order to ensure the maintenance of required community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wide &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response services. While these rate increases do not result in higher payments from Medicare and certain other public or private payors, overall they increase our net revenue.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">See &#x201C;&#x2014;Regulatory Matters&#x2014;Medicare, Medicaid and Other Government Reimbursement Programs&#x201D; for additional information on reimbursement from Medicare, Medicaid and other government</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;sponsored programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Contracts</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Emergency Transport.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;As of December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">had </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">over 245</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> contracts with communities and government agencies to provide &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response services. Contracts with communities to provide emergency transport services are typically exclusive, three to five years in length and generally are obtained through a competitive bidding process. In some instances where we are the existing provider, communities elect to renegotiate existing contracts rather than initiate new bidding processes. Our &#x201C;911&#x201D; contracts often contain options for earned extensions or evergreen provisions. In </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, our top </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &#x201C;911&#x201D; contracts accounted for approximately $</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">415</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million, or </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">23</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of AMR&#x2019;s net revenue. We have served these </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> customers on a continual basis for an average of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">35</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;years.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency response arrangements typically specify maximum fees we may charge and set forth minimum requirements, such as response times, staffing levels, types of vehicles and equipment, quality assurance and insurance coverage. Communities and government agencies may also require us to provide a performance bond or other assurances of financial responsibility. The rates we are permitted to charge for services under a contract for emergency ambulance services and the amount of the subsidy, if any, we receive from a community or government agency depend in large part on the nature of the services we provide, payor mix and performance requirements.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Emergency Transport.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have more than </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">4,800</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> arrangements to provide non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency ambulance services with hospitals, nursing homes and other healthcare facilities that require a stable and reliable source of healthcare transportation for their patients. These contracts typically designate us as the preferred ambulance service provider of non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency ambulance services to those facilities and permit us to charge a base fee, mileage reimbursement, and additional fees for the use of particular medical equipment and supplies. We have historically</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> provided a portion of our non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">emergency transports to facilities and organizations in competitive markets without specific contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency transports often are provided to managed care or insurance plan members who are stabilized at the closest available hospital and are then moved to facilities within their health plan&#x2019;s network. We believe the increased prevalence of managed care benefits larger ambulance service providers, which can service a higher percentage of a managed care provider&#x2019;s members. This allows the managed care provider to reduce its number of vendors, thus reducing administrative costs and allowing it to negotiate more favorable rates with healthcare facilities. Our scale and broad geographic footprint enable us to contract on a national and regional basis with managed care and insurance companies. We have contracts with large healthcare networks and insurers including Kaiser, Aetna, Healthnet, Cigna and SummaCare.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe that communities, government agencies, healthcare facilities, managed care companies and insurers consider the quality of care, historical response time performance and total cost to be among the most important factors in awarding and renewing contracts.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Dispatch and Communications</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Dispatch centers control the deployment and dispatch of ambulances in response to calls through the use of sophisticated communications equipment 24&nbsp;hours a day, seven days a week. In many operating sites, we communicate with our vehicles over dedicated radio frequencies licensed by the Federal Communications Commission. In certain service areas with a large volume of calls, we analyze data on traffic patterns, demographics, usage frequency and similar factors with the aid of System Status Management (&#x201C;SSM&#x201D;) technology to help determine optimal ambulance deployment and selection. In addition to dispatching our own ambulances, we also provide dispatching service for </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">67</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> communities where we are not an ambulance service provider. Our dispatch centers are staffed by EMTs and other experienced personnel who use local medical protocols to analyze and triage a medical situation and determine the best mode of transport.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Emergency Transport.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Depending on the emergency medical dispatch system used in a designated service area, the public authority that receives &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency medical calls either dispatches our ambulances directly from the public control center or communicates information regarding the location and type of medical emergency to our control </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">center which, in turn, dispatches ambulances to the scene. While the ambulance is en</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;route to the scene, the ambulance crew receives information concerning the patient&#x2019;s condition prior to the ambulance&#x2019;s arrival at the scene. Our communication systems allow the ambulance crew to communicate directly with the destination hospital to alert hospital medical personnel of the arrival of the patient and the patient&#x2019;s condition and to receive instructions directly from emergency room personnel on specific pre</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;hospital medical treatment. These systems also facilitate close and direct coordination with other emergency service providers, such as the appropriate police and fire departments, which also may be responding to a call.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Emergency Transport.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Requests for non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;emergency transports typically are made by physicians, nurses, case managers and hospital discharge coordinators who are interested primarily in prompt ambulance arrival at the requested pick</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;up time. We also offer on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;line, web</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;enabled transportation ordering to certain facilities. We use our Millennium software to track and manage requests for transportation services for large healthcare facilities and managed care companies.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Management Information Systems</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We support our operations with integrated information systems and standardized procedures that have enabled us to efficiently manage the billing and collections processes and financial support functions. Our technology solutions provide information for operations personnel, including real</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;time operating statistics, tracking of strategic plan initiatives, electronic purchasing and inventory management solutions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We have three management information systems that we believe have significantly enhanced our operations: our electronic patient care record (&#x201C;ePCR&#x201D;) technology, an electronic patient care record</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;keeping system, our Millennium call</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;taking system, a call</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;taking application that tracks and manages requests for transportation services for large healthcare facilities and managed care companies and our SSM ambulance positioning system, a technology which enables us to use historical data on fleet usage patterns to predict where our healthcare transportation services are likely to be required.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Intellectual Property</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We have registered the trademarks American Medical Response and the AMR logo and certain other trademarks and service marks in the United States. Generally, registered trademarks have perpetual life, provided that they are renewed on a timely basis and continue to be used properly as trademarks. We have registered the copyrights in our ePCR software and certain other copyrightable works. We have also developed proprietary technology that we protect through contractual provisions and confidentiality procedures and agreements. Other than the American Medical Response and AMR trademarks and the ePCR, Millennium and SSM systems, we do not believe our business is dependent to a material degree on patents, copyrights, trademarks or trade secrets. Other than licenses to commercially available software, we do not believe that any of our licenses to third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party intellectual property are material to our business taken as a whole.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Sales and Marketing</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our sales and marketing team is focused on contract retention as well as generating new sales. Many new sales opportunities occur through referrals from our existing client base. These team members are frequently former paramedics or EMTs who began their careers in the emergency transportation industry and are therefore well</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;qualified to understand the needs of our customers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We respond to RFPs that generally include demographic information of the community or facilities, response time parameters, vehicle and equipment requirements, the length of the contract, the minimum qualifications of bidders, billing information, selection criteria and the format to be followed in the bid. Prior to responding to an RFP, AMR&#x2019;s management team ensures that the proposal is in line with appropriate financial and service parameters. Management evaluates all aspects of each proposal, including financial projections, staffing models, resource requirements and competition, to determine how to best achieve our business objectives and customer goals.</font>

The inclusion of this data as part of our RFP submissions to support our clinical outcomes, as well as a recent initiative to improve and centralize our RFP writing process, has resulted in an increase in AMR&#x2019;s win rate for new &#x201C;911&#x201D; emergency services outsourcing contracts from municipalities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Risk Management</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We train and educate all new employees on our safety programs including, among others, emergency vehicle operations, various medical protocols, use of equipment and patient focused care and advocacy. Our safety training also involves continuing education programs and a monthly safety awareness campaign. We also work directly with manufacturers to design equipment modifications that enhance both patient and clinician safety.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our safety and risk management team develops and executes strategic planning initiatives focused on mitigating the factors that drive losses in our operations. We aggressively investigate and respond to incidents. Operations supervisors submit documentation of any incidents resulting in a claim to the third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party administrator handling the claim. We have a dedicated liability unit with our third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party administrator which actively engages with our staff to gain valuable information for closure of claims. Information from the claims database is an important resource for identifying trends and developing future safety initiatives.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We utilize an on</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;board monitoring system, Road Safety, which measures operator performance against our safe driving standards. Our operations using Road Safety have experienced improved driving behaviors within 90&nbsp;days of installation. Road Safety has been implemented in a significant number of our vehicles in emergency response markets. During 2011</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> we equipped our vehicles with power stretchers, which we believe reduced the number of lifting injuries to our employees in 2012 and going forward.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Competition</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our predominant competitors are fire departments and other local government providers. Based on the population of the top 200 cities, we estimate fire departments and other local government providers are approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">50</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of the ambulance transport services market. Firefighters have traditionally acted as the first responders during emergencies and in many communities provide emergency medical care and transport as well. In many communities we have established public/private partnerships, in which we integrate our transport services with the first responder services of the local fire department. We believe these public/private partnerships provide a model for us to collaborate with fire departments to increase the number of communities we serve. Based on the population of the top 200 cities, we estimate approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">48</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of communities currently </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">contract</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> ambulance serv</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ices. Of these communities</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we believe approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">67%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> contract with a local or regional provider, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% contract with a hospital</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based provider and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">23</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% contract with a national provider.</font>

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Insurance</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Workers Compensation, Auto and General Liability.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have retained liability for the first $1&nbsp;million to $3&nbsp;million of the loss under these programs since September&nbsp;1, 2001, managed either through ACE American Insurance&nbsp;Co., through an insurance subsidiary of American International Group,&nbsp;Inc., through CNA or through our Cayman</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based captive insurance subsidiary, EMCA. Generally, our umbrella policies covering claims that exceed our deductible levels have an annual cap of approximately $100&nbsp;million.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Professional Liability.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Since </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">April&nbsp;15, 2001, we have a self</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">insured retention for our professional liability coverage, which covers the first $2&nbsp;million for the policy year ending April&nbsp;15, 2002, covers the first $5 to $5.5&nbsp;million for policy periods from April&nbsp;15, 2002</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> through April&nbsp;1, 2010, and covers the first $3&nbsp;million after April&nbsp;1, 2010</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and through the present. We have umbrella policies with third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party insurers covering claims exceeding these retention levels with an aggregate cap of $10&nbsp;million to $20&nbsp;million for each separate policy period.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Environmental Matters</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We are subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations relating to the presence of hazardous materials, pollution and the protection of the environment. Such regulations include those governing emissions to air, discharges to water, storage, treatment and disposal of wastes, including medical waste, remediation of contaminated sites, and protection of worker health and safety. Non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;compliance with these requirements may result in significant fines or penalties or limitations on our operations or claims for remediation costs, as well as alleged personal injury or property damages. We believe our current operations are in substantial compliance with all applicable environmental, health and safety requirements and that we maintain all material permits required to operate our business.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Certain environmental laws impose strict, and under certain circumstances joint and several, liability for investigation and remediation of the release of regulated substances into the environment. Such liability can be imposed on current or former owners or operators of contaminated sites, or on persons who dispose or arrange for disposal of wastes at a contaminated site. Releases have occurred at a few of the facilities we lease as a result of historical practices of the owners or former operators. Based on available information, we do not believe that any known compliance obligations, releases or investigations under environmental laws or regulations will have a material adverse effect on our business, financial position and results of operations. However, there can be no guarantee that these releases or newly discovered information, more stringent enforcement of or changes in environmental requirements, or our inability to enforce available indemnification agreements will not result in significant costs.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Competitive Strengths</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We believe the following competitive strengths of Envision Healthcare position us to capitalize on the favorable healthcare services industry trends:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Leading Player in Large and Highly Fragmented Markets.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;In 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we had a total of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21.6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;million weighted patient encounters and weighted transports across approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2,200</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> communities. We are one of the largest </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">service</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> providers in our markets, though we estimate that EmCare has only a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the total ED services market, AMR has only a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of the total ambulance market, and our other services have no more than a </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% share of their respective total markets. Due to our scale and scope, we are able to offer our customers integrated services and national contracting capabilities, while demonstrating differentiated clinical outcomes across our businesses. We have developed strong brand recognition and competitive advantages in clinician recruitment as a result of our market position, clinical best practices and clinician leadership development programs. We believe that our scale and scope, when combined with our capabilities and comprehensive service offerings across the patient continuum, enable us to enter strategic business partnerships with multi</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;state hospital systems and communities, differentiating us from local and regional competitors. In addition, we believe that our track record of consistently meeting or exceeding our customers&#x2019; service expectations allows us to continue to compete effectively in the bidding process for new contracts. Given our market positions and the highly fragmented markets in which we provide our services, we believe there continue to be significant opportunities to grow market share by obtaining new contracts and through targeted acquisitions.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Differentiated Service Model Well</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Positioned for Growth.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We provide a broad set of clinically based solutions designed to enable healthcare providers, hospital systems, communities and payors to realize economic and clinical benefits. EmCare is differentiated by providing integrated physician and clinician resource management across multiple service lines, utilizing comprehensive evidence</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based clinical protocols and employing a data</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;driven process to more effectively recruit and retain physicians. AMR is differentiated by its clinical expertise, logistics management, dispatch and communication center expertise and disaster response on a local and national level. Evolution Health, which draws upon the competencies of EmCare and AMR, partners with payors, hospitals and hospitalist physicians to provide physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led coordinated care teams in multiple </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">settings. The quality and cost</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">effectiveness of care delivered by these care teams is enhanced by our medical command center for remote tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;medicine, our community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based paramedics for in</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;home patient monitoring and our transportation services for transferring patients between medical settings. Through the coordination of care among our service lines, we believe that we can deliver a differentiated offering of comprehensive care solutions across the patient continuum.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Ability to Attract and Retain High</font><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;Quality Physicians and Other Clinicians.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Through our differentiated recruiting databases and processes, we are able to identify and target high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;quality clinicians, many with a local market connection, to optimally match the needs of our facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based and community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based customers. We offer physicians and other clinicians substantial flexibility in terms of geographic location, scheduling work hours, benefit packages and opportunities for career development. We also offer clinicians the ability to provide care across the patie</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">nt continuum, including in pre</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">hospital, hospital and post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;hospital environments. We believe that our national presence and operating infrastructure enable us to provide attractive opportunities for our clinicians to enhance their skills through extensive clinical and leadership development programs. At EmCare, we have established what we believe is a highly effective medical director leadership development program. At AMR, we believe we have developed the largest paramedic and emergency medical technician training program in the country. We believe that our differentiated recruiting, training and development programs strengthen our customer and provider relationships, enhance our strong contract and clinician retention rates and allow us to efficiently recruit clinicians to support our robust new contract pipeline across each of our businesses.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Strong and Experienced Management Team with Demonstrated Track Record of Performance.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have a strong and innovative senior management team who established a track record of success while working together at our company for more than a decade. We are led by William Sanger, our Chi</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ef Executive Officer, who has 40</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;years of industry experience. 		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Strong and Consistent Revenue Growth from Diversified Sources.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have a history of delivering strong revenue growth through a combination of new contracts, same</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;contract revenue growth and acquisitions. We believe that our significant new contract revenue growth has been driven by our differentiated service offerings and abil</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ity to deliver efficient, high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">quality care. Further, new contract growth has been accelerating since 2011 as a result of our integrated service offerings and the success of each of EmCare and AMR in cross</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;selling services to their respective customers. Our new contract pipeline remains robust across</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> each of our businesses. In 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">65</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of EmCare new contracts were signed with facilities not previously utilizing our services. We believe that same</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;contract revenue growth is supported by consistent underlying market volume trends and stable pricing due to the emergency nature of many of our services. Market volumes have been driven primarily by the non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;discretionary nature of our services, aging demographics and primary care physician shortages that drive patients to emergency rooms. Furthermore, the</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> passage of the</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> PPACA </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">has led to</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> increase</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> patient volumes and provide</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">d</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> reimbursement opportunities with respect to previously uninsured patients. To supplement our same</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;contract and new contract organic growth, we have a proven track record of executing strategic acquisitions to expand our service lines and market presence.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Significant Recurring Revenue with Strong and Stable Cash Flow.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We believe that our business model and the contractual nature of our businesses drive a meaningful amount of recurring revenue. We believe that our ability to consistently deliver high levels of customer service to improve our customers&#x2019; key metrics is illustrated by our long</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;term customer relationships. The </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">10</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> largest customers at EmCare and AMR have an average tenure of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">1</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">0</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">36</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;years, respe</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">ctively. During 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">88</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of our net revenue was generated under exclusive contracts that historically have yielded high retention rates. We believe that our recurring revenue, when combined with our attractive operating margins and relatively low capital expenditure and working capital requirements, has resulted in strong and predictable cash flows. We believe that our geographic, customer, facility and service line diversification further supports the stability of our business model and cash flows.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Efficient Cost Structure and Disciplined Approach to Sustainable Growth.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We have a strong track record of achieving profitable growth, increasing operating margins and identifying cost reduction </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">opportunities. From 2010 to 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, our revenue grew at a compound annual growth rate (&#x201C;CAGR&#x201D;) of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">13.8</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">%. Over the same time period, our Adjusted EBITDA CAGR was </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">13.4</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">%, with Adjusted EBITDA margins </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">remaining consistent. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> We have improved our AMR operations by </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">deploying new technologies</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> and processes, re</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">aligning our support costs and exiting certain underperforming contracts, resulting in improved operating margins. At EmCare, we have implemented initiatives to improve physician productivity, including more efficient scheduling around peak and off</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;peak hours, use of mid</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;level providers and re</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;aligning physician compensation programs, each of which resulted in improved hospital metrics. We believe there are significant additional opportunities to improve productivity and reduce operating costs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Business Strategy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We intend to enhance our leading market positions by implementing the following key elements of our business strategy:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">26</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><hr align="center" style='background-color:#000000; border-width:0; color:#000000; height:2pt; lineheight:0; width:100%;'></hr><p style="page-break-after:always">&nbsp;</p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#Toc"><font style="display:inline;color:#0563C1;font-size:10pt;">Table of Contents</font></a>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Capitalize on Organic Growth Opportunities.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Our scale and scope, leading market positions and long operating history combined with our value</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;enhancing initiatives, provide us with competitive advantages to continue to grow our business. We intend to gain market share from local, regional and national competitors as well as through continued outsourcing of clinical services by healthcare facilities, communities and payors. We believe that EmCare is well</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;positioned to continue to generate significant organic growth due to its integrated service offerings, differentiated, data</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;driven processes to recruit and retain physicians, scalable technology and sophisticated risk management programs. We believe these factors have driven EmCare&#x2019;s strong track record in obtaining new contracts and retaining existing customers. At AMR, we believe market share gains will be driven by our strong clinical expertise, high</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;quality service, strong brand recognition and advanced information technology capabilities. In particular, our proprietary clinical database of patient transports, including detailed tracking of mortality rates and resuscitation metrics, provides analytical support to AMR&#x2019;s differentiated clinical results and has been a key factor in obtaining new contracts. We anticipate driving significant organic growth in Evolution Health by adding new contracts to meet the demand for physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led care management solutions outside the hospital.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Grow Complementary and Integrated Service Lines.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;Our continued focus on cross</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;selling and offering integrated services across the patient continuum has helped hospital systems, communities and payors to realize economic benefits and clinical value for patients. We continue to enter complementary service lines at both EmCare and AMR that leverage our core competencies. At EmCare, we continue to expand and integrate our ED, anesthesiology, hospitalist, post</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;hospital, radiology, tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;radiology and surgery </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">services. Our ability to cross</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">sell EmCare services is enhanced by our national and regional contracts that provide preferred access to certain healthcare facilities throughout the United States. In addition, our Complete Care package, which is an integrated offering of ED and hospitalist services in primarily rural communities, has been one of our most successful recent growth initiatives. These factors, among others, have increased the percentage of healthcare facilities utilizing multiple EmCare service lines from </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">11</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% in 2010</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">22% in 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. At AMR, we have expanded service lines, such as our managed transportation operations, fixed</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;wing air transportation services and community paramedic programs, with both new and existing customers. We expect Evolution Hea</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">lth to be a catalyst for cross</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">selling our services across all of our businesses and not just within a particular segment or service line.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Supplement Organic Growth with Selective Acquisitions.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;The markets in which we compete are highly fragmented, with only a few national providers. We believe we have a successful track record of completing and integrating selective acquisitions in both our EmCare and AMR segments</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">. This has</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> enhanced our presence in existing markets, facilitated our entry into new geographies and expanded the scope of our services. </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">For the eight</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;year period from 2007 through 2014, we successfully completed and integrated 38 acquisitions that were funded primarily through operating cash flows.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> In 2015</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we acquired </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">nine</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> companies for total consideration of </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">approximately $1.4</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">b</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">illion.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> We believe there are substantial opportunities for additional acquisitions across our businesses. We will continue to follow a disciplined strategy in exploring future acquisitions by analyzing the strategic rationale, financial impact and organic growth profile of each potential opportunity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Enhance Operational Efficiencies and Productivity.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We believe there continue to be significant opportunities to build upon our success in improving our productivity and profitability. At AMR, we expect to benefit from additional investments in technology aimed at improving deployment of our resources. We also expect to benefit from enhancing our ePCR billing and clinical data collection capabilities. In addition, we believe there are opportunities in areas such as optimization of field operations and fleet management. At EmCare, we continue to focus on initiatives to improve productivity. These include more efficient scheduling, continued use of mid</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;level providers, enhancing our leadership training programs and improving and re</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;aligning compensation programs. Furthermore, in both segments, we will continue to utilize risk mitigation programs for loss prevention and early intervention including continued use of clinical &#x201C;fail</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;safes&#x201D; and technology and equipment in ambulances to reduce vehicular incidents and lifting injuries. We believe that our significant investments in scalable technology systems will facilitate additional cost reductions and efficiencies. Opportunities include improved efficiencies in the deployment of our ambulance resources, enhancing our risk</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;mitigation program, improving billing/collection cycle times and reducing costs with the implementation of electronic medical record systems at our client facilities.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Expand our Evolution Health Business.</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> &nbsp;We believe that our strong market positions in integrated facility</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based physician services and community</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;based healthcare transportation services uniquely position us to provide </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led care management solutions outside the hospital. We offer an attractive value proposition through our business model which helps payors reduce their cost of care, promote the most appropriate care in the most appropriate setting, identify member health risks, enable self</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;care and independence at home, and reduce hospital lengths of stay and readmissions. For hospitals, we believe our business model can improve patient flow coordination, decrease lengths of stay and reduce readmission rates. We are implementing our strategy by first utilizing analytics to identify eligible patients and then employing multiple techniques and physician</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;led services to manage the quality and cost of patient care, including transitional care teams, direct patient care and care coordination by clinicians outside the acute</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;care setting, tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;monitoring and tele</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;medicine.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-size:10pt;">Regulatory Matters</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Our </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">operations and relationships with</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> allied</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> healthcare providers such as hospitals, other healthcare facilities and healthcare professionals are subject to extensive and increasing regulation by numerous federal and state government entities as well as local government agencies. Specifically, but without limitation, we are subject to the following laws and regulations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;font-size:10pt;">Medicare, Medicaid and Other Government Reimbursement Programs</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">We derive a significant portion of our revenue from services rendered to beneficiaries of Medicare, Medicaid and other government</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;sponsored healthcare programs. For 201</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">5</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, we received approximately 2</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">6</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% of our net revenue from Medicare and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">9</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">% from Medicaid. To participate in these programs, we must comply with stringent and often complex enrollment and reimbursement requirements from the federal and state governments. We are subject to governmental reviews and audits of our bills and claims for reimbursement. Retroactive adjustments to amounts previously reimbursed from these programs can and do occur on a regular basis as a result of these reviews and audits. Additionally, prepayment reviews, auto denial edits and prepayment investigations can also occur. These programs are subject to statutory and regulatory changes, administrative rulings, interpretations and determinations, all of which may materially increase or decrease the payments we receive for our services as well as affect the cost of providing services. In recent years, Congress has consistently attempted to curb federal spending on such programs.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Reimbursement to us typically is conditioned on our providing the correct procedure and diagnosis codes and properly documenting both the service itself and the medical necessity for the service. Incorrect or incomplete documentation and billing information, or the incorrect selection of codes for the level of service provided, could result in non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;payment for services rendered or lead to allegations of billing fraud. Moreover, third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors may disallow, in whole or in part, requests for reimbursement based on determinations that certain amounts are not reimbursable, they were for services provided that were not medically necessary, there was a lack of sufficient supporting documentation, or for a number of other reasons. Retroactive adjustments, recoupments or refund demands may change amounts realized from third</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;party payors. Additional factors that could complicate our billing include:</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;color:#000000;">the difficulty of adherence to specific compliance requirements, diagnosis coding and various other procedures mandated by the government, and</font></p></td></tr></table></div>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Due to the nature of our business and our participation in the Medicare and Medicaid reimbursement programs, we are involved from time to time in regulatory reviews, audits or investigations by government agencies of matters such as compliance with billing regulations and rules. We may be required to repay these agencies if a determination is made that we were incorrectly reimbursed, or we may lose eligibility for certain programs in the event of certain types of non</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;compliance. Delays and uncertainties in the reimbursement process adversely affect our level of accounts receivable, increase the overall cost of collection, and may adversely affect our working capital and cause us to incur additional borrowing costs. Unfavorable resolutions of pending or future regulatory reviews or investigations, either individually or in the aggregate, could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">28</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font>
