		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 0pt 18pt;text-indent:18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">The Company is organized around </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">two</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> separately managed business units: facility-based and post-acute care physician services and healthcare transportation services, which have been identified as reportable operating segments. The facility-based and post-acute care physician services reportable segment provides physician services to hospitals primarily for emergency department, anesthesiology, hospitalist/inpatient, radiology, tele-radiology and surgery services. It also offers physician-led care management solutions outside the hospital. The healthcare transportation services reportable segment focuses on providing a full range of medical transportation services from basic patient transit to the most advanced emergency care and pre-hospital assistance. The Chief Executive Officer has been identified as the chief operating decision maker (the &#x201C;CODM&#x201D;) as he assesses the performance of the business units and decides how to allocate resources to the business units.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Net income (loss) before equity in earnings of unconsolidated subsidiary, income tax benefit (expense), loss on early debt extinguishment, other income (expense), net, realized gains (losses) on investments, interest expense, net, equity-based compensation expense, transaction costs related to acquisition activity, related party management fees, restructuring and other charges, severance and related costs, adjustment to net (income) loss attributable to noncontrolling interest due to deferred taxes, and depreciation and amortization expense (&#x201C;Adjusted EBITDA&#x201D;) is the measure of profit and loss that the CODM uses to assess performance and make decisions. Adjusted EBITDA is not considered a measure of financial performance under GAAP and the items excluded from Adjusted EBITDA are significant components in understanding and assessing the Company&#x2019;s financial performance. Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as an alternative to such GAAP measures as net income, cash flows provided by or used in operating, investing or financing activities or other financial statement data presented in the Company&#x2019;s financial statements as an indicator of financial performance. Since Adjusted EBITDA is not a measure </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">45%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of AMR employees are represented by </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">70</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> active collective bargaining agreements. There are </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">29</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> operational locations representing approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">4,160</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> employees currently in the process of negotiations or will be subject to </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">negotiation</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> in 2016. In addition, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">18</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> collective bargaining agreements, representing approximately </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">2,540</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> employees will be subject to negotiations in 2017. While the Company believes it maintains a good working relationship with its employees, the Company has experienced some union work actions. The Company does not expect these actions to have a material adverse effect on its ability to provide service to its patients and communities.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">One</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> customer, </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Hospital</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> Corporation of America, comprised </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">24.1%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, &nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">27.5%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">, and </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">21.7%</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> of EmCare&#x2019;s total net revenue as of December 31, 2015, 2014 and 2013, respectively. 			<font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Envision Healthcare Holdings,&nbsp;Inc. (the &#x201C;Parent&#x201D;) was incorporated in Delaware on February&nbsp;28, 2011</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">,</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;"> in connection with the merger of CDRT Merger Sub,&nbsp;Inc., a wholly</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;owned subsidiary of Envision Healthcare Intermediate Corporation, a wholly</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">&#8209;owned subsidiary of Parent, with and into Envision Healthcare Corporation (&#x201C;Corporation&#x201D;). The Parent has no significant operations or assets other than its indirect ownership of the equity of Corporation. Accordingly, the Parent is dependent upon distributions from Corporation to fund its obligations. However, under the terms of Corporation&#x2019;s credit agreements governing Corporation&#x2019;s ABL Facility and Term Loan and the Indenture governing Corporation&#x2019;s 20</font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">22 </font><font style="display:inline;font-size:10pt;">Notes, Corporation&#x2019;s ability to pay dividends or lend to the Parent is restricted, except that Corporation may pay specified amounts to Parent to fund the payment of the Company&#x2019;s tax obligations. Corporation has no obligation to pay dividends to Parent.</font>
